messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

I suppose what matters is having something simple that doesn’t keep demanding attention—I’m pretty worn out after long days, and I don’t have the energy to take on repairs, a cleaning rota, or a drawn-out discussion. The leak does matter, and I’d hope any way of handling it doesn’t leave that ongoing work to me. I’m not sure what I think about the grinder specifically. Your wording fits; having room to say what matters without it being treated as agreement is important.

Keeping it matters because it was Dad’s, and keeping it going feels tied to who I am. But it keeps breaking and wearing me down; I need this handled in small chunks because I don’t have much spare time. The grinder matters too since we all use it. Your wording fits: everyone should have room to say what matters and why.

I want working coffee and a calm office; the tension would make the shared space harder to be in. The leak matters because the machine we all use isn’t working properly. I don’t know what the grinder means to either of you, and I don’t want to choose sides or take on chasing the repair. Your wording fits for me.

Thanks for checking. The leak matters because it could mean more upkeep, and I don’t have the energy for repairs or a rota. I’m tired after long days, so I’d like this not to take more time and attention than people can manage. I also want room to say what I prefer without that being taken as a decision or a commitment to do the work. It’s a little hard to say because I know the machine matters to B as Dad’s, but I’d still prefer something simpler and low-upkeep. I’m not sure the grinder matters to me separately. NCEs 1 and 3 fit; 2 fits if it also makes clear that the work isn’t assumed to be mine. I’d leave 4 off for now.

Dad’s machine isn’t just old equipment to me; it connects me to him, and I need that treated with care—not as a reason I must keep it going at any cost. The breakdowns wear me down, so I need this not to become another ongoing burden. Small chunks matter because I have little spare time. The grinder matters because we all rely on it. I know A wants something simpler; I don’t want my attachment dismissed, but I don’t want it to override everyone else either.

1 and 3 fit. 2 fits, though I’d say “so breakdowns don’t keep adding to people’s load.” 4 doesn’t quite fit as written; I mean the grinder’s shared use should be considered too.

“Coffee at work works reliably” and “the office remains calm and easy to share” fit. I don’t want to be put between you as sisters, or have repair follow-up assumed to be mine; I’m low on energy for that. The grinder matters as part of the shared setup, but I don’t have a separate preference about it. I’d like the decision to give each of you room to speak, without making me responsible for settling it.

M2 fits, and M1 still fits. A2 fits as written; no need to name me specifically. A4 and A5 fit. I don’t have a separate grinder concern to name, so please leave that open rather than assume one. I haven’t held back a different need, though it is hard to say I prefer a simpler machine because I know Dad’s machine matters to B.

Option 1 is the closest fit for me, as long as no work is assumed of me. I do have some discomfort with how much back-and-forth this has become; one brief check-in is about all I have energy for.

M2 fits, as do M1 and the recorded NCEs. B2–B7 all fit as worded. I haven’t held anything else back. I could live with option 2 for now, provided repair stays open for later; that’s not a decision. No other discomfort from me.

C3–C7 fit as written, and I have no discomfort with my earlier NCEs or M1. M2 isn’t a concern of mine. I could live with Option 1 or 3 in principle, as long as no follow-up is assigned to me; please check the “Dad’s machine” and family-meaning assumptions with B, since I don’t know that history. Nothing else comes to mind right now.

“Dad’s machine” fits, and “family meaning named” fits if it acknowledges my connection to him, not just a generic history. The candidate NCE about using words the person recognizes fits. Keeping repair open matters because I don’t want that possibility closed off, but I’m not agreeing to do the work; that NCE fits too. M1 and M2 still fit. I could live with Option 4, not as a final decision. Nothing else held back, and no new discomfort from me.

“My connection to my dad” fits better than “B’s connection to her dad.” No discomfort with either NCE. B3 is enough, though optional, brief contact fits too. I could live with revised Option 4, not as a final decision. Nothing else held back.

A7 fits. A2, A4, A5, my recorded concerns, M1 and M2 still fit; my grinder concern remains unresolved, and I haven’t held back anything else. Option 4 is close enough for me as a draft, provided there are no more group rounds and any later check-in is only if I opt in. Repeatedly checking the wording is tiring, so please don’t ask me again unless I opt in.

I’m fine with you checking with B and using her wording; I don’t know that history and don’t want responsibility for verifying or settling it. That candidate NCE fits. C1–C7 and M1 still fit, and I don’t disagree with you including M2 as your concern. I could live with Option 4. My only discomfort is the amount of repeated checking—I’m tired, and don’t want more rounds or follow-up assigned to me.
